question_stem:
Carbon-15 ($^{15}_{6}\text{C}$) is an isotope of carbon that undergoes radioactive decay to nitrogen-15 ($^{15}_{7}\text{N}$), which is a stable isotope of nitrogen.

Radioactive decay is both a random and a spontaneous process.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State how Fig. 10.1 demonstrates that radioactive decay is random.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 10.1, draw the straight line of best fit.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Show that the decay constant $\lambda$ of carbon-15 is given by the magnitude of the gradient of your line in (b)(ii).

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use your line in (b)(ii) to determine $\lambda$. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (b)(v)
parts.text: Use your answer in (b)(iv) to calculate the half-life of carbon-15.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The equation for the decay of carbon-15 can be written as

$$^{15}_{6}\text{C} \rightarrow ^{15}_{7}\text{N} + ^{0}_{-1}\beta + ^{0}_{0}\bar{\nu}.$$

State and explain how the mass of the products of the decay must compare with the mass of the carbon-15 nucleus.
